stories.headline: Tencent-backed Enflame closes up 179% in Shanghai debut after $912M AI-chip IPO

key_facts.fact: Shanghai Enflame Technology (688801.SS) closed 179% higher on its Shanghai debut on Friday, Sept 11, after raising 6.12 billion yuan ($912 million) in its IPO.
key_facts.excerpt: Chinese artificial intelligence chipmaker Shanghai Enflame Technology closed up 179% in its Shanghai debut on Friday, after the Tencent-backed company raised 6.12 billion yuan ($912 million) in its initial public offering.

key_facts.fact: The stock opened at 410 yuan versus an offer price of 142.18 yuan, hit a high of 475 yuan and closed at 397 yuan; Enflame sold 43.04 million new shares, equal to 10% of its enlarged share capital, on the STAR Market.
key_facts.excerpt: The stock opened at 410 yuan, well above its offer price of 142.18 yuan, hit a high of 475 yuan and a low of 386.99 yuan, before closing at 397 yuan... Enflame sold 43.04 million new shares, equal to 10% of its enlarged share capital.

key_facts.fact: The debut gave Enflame a market capitalisation of 176.4 billion yuan (about US$26.3 billion); the retail portion of the IPO was oversubscribed 4,073 times, with roughly 7 million individual investors ordering 42.1 billion shares and an allocation rate of 0.025%.
key_facts.excerpt: giving the Tencent Holdings-backed artificial intelligence chipmaker a market capitalisation of 176.4 billion yuan... The retail portion of its initial public offering (IPO) was oversubscribed by 4,073 times, with about 7 million online investors alone submitting orders for 42.1 billion shares. The allocation rate for individual investors was just 0.025 per cent.

key_facts.fact: Enflame is the last of China's 'four little dragons' of AI chipmaking to go public, alongside Moore Threads, Biren Technology and MetaX, and says it will use proceeds to develop and commercialise its fifth- and sixth-generation AI chips.
key_facts.excerpt: Enflame is the last of China's 'four little dragons' of AI chipmaking to go public... Enflame said it plans to use proceeds from the listing to develop and commercialize its fifth- and sixth-generation AI chips, as it seeks to match the performance of high-end products from international rivals.

key_facts.fact: Shares rallied as much as 234% intraday, minting two billionaires: chairman Zhao Lidong, 60, and CEO Zhang Yalin, 48, each with a fortune Forbes estimates at $2.1 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: the two cofounders of chipmaker Shanghai Enflame Technology joining the world's three-comma club on Friday as the company's shares rallied as much as 234% in its trading debut... The two newly minted billionaires are Enflame's 60-year-old Chairman Zhao Lidong and 48-year-old CEO Zhang Yalin. Each has amassed a fortune of $2.1 billion.

key_facts.fact: The listing valued the firm at about 61 billion yuan before trading began, making it one of the largest mainland Chinese tech listings of the year, and reflects Beijing's push for domestic alternatives as the US restricts Nvidia exports.
key_facts.excerpt: The offering valued the firm at about 61 billion yuan before trading began, making it one of the largest tech listings in mainland China this year... Beijing's push for semiconductor self-sufficiency as the US restricts exports of advanced chips from global leaders such as Nvidia.

stories.headline: Microsoft plans to more than triple data center capacity to 38GW by 2032

key_facts.fact: Microsoft plans to expand its data center network to more than 38 gigawatts of capacity in 2032, up from about 12 gigawatts today, after shortages forced it to turn away some AI and cloud business.
key_facts.excerpt: The company's globe-spanning network of data centers will have more than 38 gigawatts of capacity in 2032, up from about 12 gigawatts now, according to people familiar with the plans. That would eclipse the amount of electricity New York state uses during peak periods.

key_facts.fact: Only about 2 gigawatts of Microsoft's current 12-gigawatt capacity is centered on AI-specific chips, a share expected to grow to about a third of the planned 38 gigawatts.
key_facts.excerpt: According to the report only about 2 gigawatts of the company's current 12-gigawatt capacity is centered on AI-specific chips, a share expected to grow to about a third of the 38 gigawatts it plans to have online.

key_facts.fact: Microsoft is planning to spread long-term data center leases over 25 years rather than 15, which lowers its annual reported capital expenditures.
key_facts.excerpt: The company is planning to spread long-term leases on data centers over 25 years rather than 15, which has the effect of lowering its annual reported capital expenditures.

key_facts.fact: The target covers owned and leased facilities but excludes compute rented from neoclouds such as CoreWeave, and has not been confirmed by Microsoft in any release or filing.
key_facts.excerpt: The target covers company-owned and leased facilities but excludes computing power rented from neoclouds such as CoreWeave... Microsoft has not confirmed the figure in a release or filing, and the plan comes from unnamed sources rather than the company.

key_facts.fact: Reaching 38GW would require adding about 26 gigawatts and growing AI-focused capacity more than sixfold, to roughly 12.7 gigawatts; Microsoft expects capital expenditures of $50 billion in fiscal Q1 2027 and $175 billion during calendar 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Microsoft's reported target would add about 26 GW of capacity and increase its AI-focused fleet more than sixfold... That implies about 12.7 gigawatts of AI-focused capacity, more than six times the current figure... Reuters reported that Microsoft expects capital expenditures of $50 billion in its fiscal first quarter of 2027 and $175 billion during calendar 2026.

key_facts.fact: The plan reverses course from earlier in 2026, when Microsoft walked away from roughly 2 gigawatts of planned US and European projects amid analyst warnings of AI compute oversupply.
key_facts.excerpt: Earlier in 2026, the company walked away from roughly 2 gigawatts of planned American and European projects, a pullback analysts at TD Cowen attributed to oversupply of AI compute clusters. Months later it is planning to more than triple total capacity.

stories.headline: Pentagon in talks to lend about $5B to AI data-center builder Fluidstack

key_facts.fact: The Pentagon is in talks to lend roughly $5 billion to AI cloud-computing startup Fluidstack to shore up the US data-center supply chain, the Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday, Sept 10.
key_facts.excerpt: The Pentagon is in talks to lend roughly $5 billion to AI cloud-computing startup Fluidstack to shore up the U.S. data-center supply chain, the Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter.

key_facts.fact: The financing would come from the Department of Defense's Office of Strategic Capital and would be that office's largest loan to date; no loan has been signed or closed.
key_facts.excerpt: The Wall Street Journal reported on September 10th that the proposed financing would come from the Department of Defense's Office of Strategic Capital. The transaction remains under discussion, and the Journal did not report a signed or closed loan. If approved at the reported size, it would be the office's largest loan to date.

key_facts.fact: The money would primarily fund US manufacturing capacity for data-center power and cooling equipment rather than a single new facility.
key_facts.excerpt: the money wouldn't primarily bankroll a shiny new data center: it would help build US supply-chain and manufacturing capacity for specific data-center components, the 'picks and shovels' that determine how fast new facilities can actually come online.

key_facts.fact: Fluidstack's loan application is being advised by Erebor Bank, the national bank founded by Palmer Luckey that received its charter in February 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Fluidstack's loan application is being advised by Erebor Bank, the Wall Street Journal reported. That name matters because Palmer Luckey is behind it... Erebor received a US national bank charter in February 2026 to serve companies in AI, defense, crypto and manufacturing, according to Reuters.

key_facts.fact: Fluidstack, founded in London in 2017 by Gary Wu and Jamie Cox and headquartered in New York since December 2025, raised an $830 million Series A at a $7.5 billion valuation and a later $1.5 billion round led by Jane Street valuing it above $18 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Founded in London in 2017, Fluidstack shifted its global headquarters to New York in December 2025... Fluidstack raised an $830 million Series A at a $7.5 billion valuation earlier this year. A subsequent $1.5 billion financing led by Jane Street reportedly valued the company at more than $18 billion.

key_facts.fact: Fluidstack is a core infrastructure partner for Anthropic's announced $50 billion US compute build-out, with data centers in New York and Texas designed for Anthropic's workloads.
key_facts.excerpt: The company has become a major infrastructure partner for Anthropic, which announced a $50 billion US computing build-out using Fluidstack data centres in New York and Texas.

stories.headline: d-Matrix licenses Nvidia's NVLink Fusion to plug its Raptor inference chips into Nvidia racks

key_facts.fact: AI inference chipmaker d-Matrix announced on Sept 10 it will use Nvidia NVLink Fusion to connect its next-generation Raptor XPUs to Nvidia's AI infrastructure platform.
key_facts.excerpt: AI inference chipmaker d-Matrix today announced it will use NVIDIA NVLink Fusion to connect its next-generation Raptor XPUs to NVIDIA's AI infrastructure platform — joining a growing roster of ecosystem partners.

key_facts.fact: The collaboration includes a multi-year product roadmap and an NVLink Fusion-enabled rack built on Nvidia's MGX architecture with Vera CPUs, NVLink switches, BlueField-4 DPUs, ConnectX-9 SuperNICs and Spectrum-X Ethernet; d-Matrix is also partnering with Astera Labs.
key_facts.excerpt: d-Matrix today announced a new collaboration with NVIDIA that includes a multi-year product roadmap... incorporate d-Matrix's next-gen inference XPUs, starting with d-Matrix Raptor, directly into the latest NVIDIA rack reference architecture design featuring NVIDIA Vera CPUs, NVIDIA NVLink switches, NVIDIA BlueField-4 DPUs, NVIDIA ConnectX-9 SuperNICs, and NVIDIA Spectrum-X Ethernet networking. d-Matrix is also partnering with Astera Labs.

key_facts.fact: Raptor is expected to tape out before the end of 2026, with initial availability of Raptor XPUs integrated into the Nvidia MGX rack expected in Q4 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: d-Matrix has designed Raptor, which is expected to tape-out before the end of the year... Initial availability of d-Matrix Raptor XPUs integrated into the NVIDIA MGX rack is expected Q4 2027.

key_facts.fact: d-Matrix joins Qualcomm, Arm, Marvell, Amazon, Fujitsu and MediaTek as NVLink Fusion licensees; Nvidia invested $3.5 billion in MediaTek as part of last week's deal and $2 billion to bring Marvell in.
key_facts.excerpt: AI infrastructure startup joins Qualcomm, Arm, Marvell, Amazon, Fujitsu, and MediaTek as NVLink true believers... As part of the MediaTek deal last week, Nvidia invested $3.5 billion in the SoC designer, while it spent $2 billion to get Marvell in the door.

key_facts.fact: d-Matrix CEO Sid Sheth said in a press briefing that NVLink Fusion and MGX let the company integrate Raptor into a broadly deployed liquid-cooled architecture for ultralow-latency inference.
key_facts.excerpt: "Demand for inference is soaring, but capital, time and energy remain finite," said Sid Sheth, cofounder and CEO of d-Matrix during a press briefing yesterday. "With NVLink Fusion and MGX, we can integrate our Raptor XPUs into a broadly deployed, liquid-cooled architecture."

stories.headline: Ayar Labs adds $150M, taking 2026 funding to $650M for co-packaged optics

key_facts.fact: Ayar Labs said on Thursday, Sept 10, that it raised an additional $150 million, an extension of the $500 million Series E it announced in March, bringing total primary capital raised in 2026 to $650 million.
key_facts.excerpt: Ayar Labs, a Silicon Valley startup developing a way to link AI chips directly together with optical connections, on Thursday said it has raised an additional $150 million. The fresh capital is an extension of a series E $500 million funding round the company announced in March.

key_facts.fact: The extension takes Ayar Labs past $1 billion in total outside funding; the March round was led by Neuberger Berman with Nvidia, AMD and MediaTek participating.
key_facts.excerpt: The company originally disclosed it had raised $500 million in its Series E round back in March, which was led by Neuberger Berman. Nvidia Corp., Advanced Micro Devices Inc. and MediaTek Inc. also participated in that round, which brought its total amount raised to $870 million. With today's Series E extension, Ayar Labs has now raised just over a billion dollars in outside funding.

key_facts.fact: Ayar separately disclosed that Taiwanese data-center infrastructure maker Wiwynn made a strategic investment earlier this year, joining backers Alchip, AMD, Intel, MediaTek and Nvidia.
key_facts.excerpt: Separately, it discloses that Wiwynn made a strategic investment earlier this year. Wiwynn, a cloud IT and infrastructure provider for data centers, joins a growing group of strategic backers that includes Alchip, AMD, Intel, MediaTek, and NVIDIA.

key_facts.fact: CEO and co-founder Mark Wade said copper interconnect is becoming the limiting factor for AI scale-up and the money funds manufacturing-ready co-packaged optics, product validation and a new Bengaluru Design Center in India.
key_facts.excerpt: "Copper interconnect is becoming the limiting factor for AI scale-up," said Mark Wade, CEO and co-founder of Ayar Labs. "This funding allows us to move faster on manufacturing-ready co-packaged optics at scale."... supports product development, manufacturing ecosystem readiness, high-volume production, and new Bengaluru Design Center in India.

key_facts.fact: Wade told Reuters the company aims to bring the technology to mass market by early 2028 and said all products must be qualified for volume production by the end of 2027 to match customer ramps in 2028-2029.
key_facts.excerpt: Wade told Reuters the company now hopes to bring its technology to the mass market by early 2028... "If my customer's products are looking to ramp in the 2028-2029 time frame, we have to have all of our stuff qualified for volume production by the end of 2027."

key_facts.fact: Ayar's TeraPHY optical engine sits in the ASIC socket alongside the processor, replacing copper links that overheat over distance and capping how large GPU clusters can be.
key_facts.excerpt: Ayar Labs' TeraPHY replaces copper with optical connectivity that delivers the bandwidth, performance, power efficiency, and low latency needed to connect large GPU clusters across racks and data centers. By leveraging co-packaged optics (CPO), Ayar places optical engines like the TeraPHY Optical Engine directly into the ASIC socket alongside the processor.

stories.headline: Silver Lake and Intel-backed Altera prepares IPO that could raise over $2 billion

key_facts.fact: Altera, the FPGA chipmaker backed by Silver Lake and Intel, is preparing an IPO that could raise over $2 billion as early as 2026, Reuters reported on Sept 10.
key_facts.excerpt: Silver Lake and Intel-backed chipmaker Altera is preparing for an initial public offering that could raise over $2 billion as early as 2026, according to people familiar with the matter, in one of the largest semiconductor listings in recent years.

key_facts.fact: Silver Lake has tapped Barclays, Citi, JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley as underwriters, with the bank order not yet finalized.
key_facts.excerpt: Silverlake has tapped Barclays, Citi, JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley as underwriters for the Altera IPO, however, the order of banks in the lineup is yet to be finalized, three of the sources said.

key_facts.fact: The San Jose-based company is preparing to file confidentially in the coming weeks, with a listing possible as early as this year; timing and size could still change.
key_facts.excerpt: The San Jose, California-based company, is preparing to confidentially file for the IPO in the coming weeks and a listing could come as early as this year, the sources said, cautioning the plans, including the timing and size of the offering, could still change.

key_facts.fact: Intel bought Altera for about $16.7 billion in 2015; Altera became fully standalone last September after Intel sold a 51% stake to Silver Lake for $4.46 billion at an $8.75 billion valuation, with Intel retaining 49%.
key_facts.excerpt: The company was acquired by Intel for about $16.7 billion in 2015 and became fully standalone last September after Intel agreed to sell a 51 per cent stake to Silver Lake for $4.46 billion in a transaction valuing the chipmaker at $8.75 billion. Intel retains a 49 per cent stake.

key_facts.fact: Silver Lake committed about $3.3 billion in equity to the deal alongside Abu Dhabi's MGX as co-investor.
key_facts.excerpt: Silver Lake committed about $3.3 billion in equity to the transaction alongside Abu Dhabi-based investment firm MGX, which participated as a co-investor.

key_facts.fact: A listing would let Intel mark its 49% stake to market as CEO Lip-Bu Tan restructures the company; Altera CEO Raghib Hussain said in a July interview the company was preparing for an eventual IPO as it pursues AI and robotics markets.
key_facts.excerpt: Altera CEO Raghib Hussain has previously expressed interest in taking the company public. In a July interview, he said the company was 'preparing for an eventual IPO' as it pursues growth in the AI and robotics markets... If Altera's listing proceeds, the value of Intel's 49% stake would be marked to market.

stories.headline: Huang defends Nvidia's investments as 'not circular' and reaffirms 70% revenue growth

key_facts.fact: Speaking at the Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference on Thursday, Sept 10, Jensen Huang rejected the circular-financing critique: 'It's not circular because we put a little bit of money in, and a lot of money comes back... We put in one, and a hundred comes back in. Is that circular? If that is, let's do more of that.'
key_facts.excerpt: "It's not circular because we put a little bit of money in, and a lot of money comes back," Huang said Thursday to laughter. He added: "We put in one, and a hundred comes back in. Is that circular? If that is, let's do more of that."

key_facts.fact: Huang reaffirmed guidance of roughly 70% revenue growth next year while saying unconstrained demand growth exceeds 100%, and said Nvidia is turning compute 'from technology to an investable asset' in work with the financial industry.
key_facts.excerpt: 70% revenue growth next year, unconstrained demand growth of over 100%... We are moving NVIDIA Compute from technology to an investable asset.

key_facts.fact: He said $400 billion of venture funding went into AI-native companies in the last six months, defining an AI native as a company that spends two-thirds of its raised money on compute: 'There is no such thing as a low CapEx software company anymore.'
key_facts.excerpt: $400 billion of VC funding went into AI natives in the last six months. $400 billion. AI natives, the definition of an AI native is somebody who spends two-thirds of their raised money on compute. There is no such thing as a low CapEx software company anymore.

key_facts.fact: Huang dismissed the current wave of AI-danger warnings as demand creation for security products: 'What better way to create demand than to create a problem?... Who doesn't want their market to be hysterical about their product?' — calling cybersecurity AI's next major use case.
key_facts.excerpt: "What better way to create demand than to create a problem," Huang told the crowd at a Goldman Sachs conference in San Francisco before questioning: "Who doesn't want their market to be hysterical about their product and line up around the corner for it?" The billionaire said "the industry is getting ready to launch some products."

key_facts.fact: He argued 'In AI, compute is revenue', and Nvidia's disclosures show three direct customers accounted for 16%, 15% and 13% of revenue in the first half of fiscal 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: "In AI, compute is revenue," he said, arguing that Nvidia's chips function as productive, revenue-generating assets rather than one-time hardware sales... Nvidia's own SEC disclosures add some texture to the concentration question, showing three direct customers accounted for 16%, 15% and 13% of revenue in the first half of fiscal 2027.

key_facts.fact: Huang also said AI infrastructure spending could reach $3 trillion to $4 trillion by 2030 and cited constraints in packaging, DRAM, connectors, voltage regulators and wafers.
key_facts.excerpt: Speaking at the Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference, Huang reiterated his view that AI infrastructure spending could reach $3 trillion to $4 trillion by 2030... On AI infrastructure constraints, Huang cited challenges involving packaging, DRAM, connectors, voltage regulators and wafers.
